newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dlr/yen vol curve, risk reversals flip.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr/yen vol curve, risk reversals flip.

text.p: Shorter-dated dollar/yen options, particularly yen calls, were bid up in U.S. trading as the dollar plunged more than four yen from overnight highs to the mid-114-yen area, dealers said.

As a result, the volatility curve, which had been positively sloped for several weeks, inverted and risk reversals, the put/call pricing differential, flipped in favor of yen calls in the shorter maturities.
Dollar/mark volatilities were little changed, however, even though spot dollar/mark also skidded nearly four pfennig to the 1.84-mark area, traders added.
"Yen calls are very qiuck to go bid historically," a European bank trader in Chicago said.

Japanese exporters, who had been content to sit on the sidelines for the past several weeks while the dollar retraced its May-June losses, rushed back to cover their dollar exposures, traders said. Short positions in yen calls that had recently accumulated due to yen put buying through risk reversals also induced short-covering.
One-month dollar/yen volatility was up a quarter point at 12.2/12.5 percent in late trade. The back end was steadier, with six-month to one-year at around 11.9/12.2 percent.
One-month 25-delta risk reversal was favoring yen calls by about 0.3/0.5 point by mid-afternoon, compared with a 0.4/0.7 point skew toward yen puts late on Thursday.
"Obviously, everyone's excited about the dollar's downside again after today's move," said Ted Voorhees, a senior trader at Deutsche Bank in New York.

The 120-yen level has proved to be a strong barrier after the dollar stalled at 119.58 yen on Wednesday, and the long-dated low-delta yen puts that had been the flavor of the month in July and early August were quickly losing luster, traders said.
By comparison, dollar/mark volatilities were barely changed, at 11.3/11.5 percent from one-month out to one-year.

"Risk reversals clearly favored the dollar's upside, and vols were extremely well-bid in anticipation of breaking 1.90 (marks)," Voorhees explained. "So obviously, with a lower dollar...there's not as much as nervousness."
The dollar had been on a relentless one-way advance for months before losing steam at 1.8913 marks on Wednesday.
"It looks like we've finally established the upper end of this trading range," Voorhees said. "It's the first time we've actually seen a pullback."
"I think a better question is why volatilities haven't come lower," he added.
Traders said dollar/mark volatilities could pick up if spot either fell further or bounced to resume the uptrend.

A Japanese bank dealer said odds still favored a higher dollar, pointing at mark/yen's steady downtrend and liklihood that the dollar/yen's downside would be limited. Spot mark/yen plumbed new two-year lows again today to just above 62 yen.
Elsewhere, sterling volatilities remained firm as the pound continued testing the downside. One-month cable stood at 10.5/10.8 percent, up a quarter point.
